\section[\texorpdfstring{\te{గుంట} (guṇṭa)}{గుంట (guṇṭa)}]{\te{గుంట} (guṇṭa) — a pit, a pothole}

\label{lesson:TE-C308-gunta}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for an incense stick, then the Telugu for kumkum.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{గుంట}}
\textbf{\te{గుంట}} — \emph{guṇṭa} — \textquotedblleft{}a pit, a pothole\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\te{గుంట}} (\emph{guṇṭa}) is native Dravidian. DEDR 1669 lists \emph{guṇṭa}, \textquotedblleft{}pit, pond\textquotedblright{}, with Tamil \emph{kuṇṭu}, \textquotedblleft{}hollow, pit\textquotedblright{}, and Kannada \emph{kuṇṭe}, \textquotedblleft{}pit\textquotedblright{}. DEDR compares Sanskrit \emph{kuṇḍa}, \textquotedblleft{}pit, well\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 3264), which CDIAL takes from Dravidian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{guṇṭa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{guṇṭa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{guṇṭa}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Telugu for an incense stick, then the Telugu for kumkum, then say \emph{guṇṭa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \te{గుంట} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A pit, a pothole\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\te{అంచు} (añcu)}{అంచు (añcu)}]{\te{అంచు} (añcu) — an edge, a rim}

\label{lesson:TE-C308-ancu}

\textbf{\te{అంచు}} — \emph{añcu} — \textquotedblleft{}an edge, a rim\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\te{అంచు}} (\emph{añcu}) is Dravidian. DEDR 57 lists \emph{añcu}, \textquotedblleft{}border, edge, brim\textquotedblright{}, with Kannada \emph{añcu}, \textquotedblleft{}edge\textquotedblright{}, and notes that Tamil \emph{aṉsu} was borrowed from Telugu. DEDR compares Sanskrit \emph{añcala}, \textquotedblleft{}border of a garment\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 168).
